history.summary: The 'Battisa' (Hindi for thirty-two) temple: an east-facing Shiva temple built on a 3-foot-high platform, with two rectangular sanctum sanctorums — housing Shivalingas named Someshwara and Gangadeshwara — joined by a single mandapam of 32 stone pillars in 4 rows by 8 columns; a circumbulatory path runs around each sanctum and a Nandi faces each. The shikhara over the sanctums is completely destroyed and the walls are devoid of ornament; a relief of Ganesha sits on the sanctum lintel. Its inscription dates it to 1209 AD (Shaka 1130), built by Ganga Mahadevi, queen of the Nagavanshi ruler Someshwara Deva — one shrine named Someshwara after her husband, the other Gangadeshwara — who donated Keramruka village for the temple's upkeep (the inscription is now preserved in the Nagpur museum). Geological study of the site notes visible earthquake damage to the structure. ASI-protected monument. (CSV town 'Jagdalpur' is wrong — the temple is at Barsur in Dantewada district. Coordinates approximate — sources conflict between ~19.13/81.38 and 19°07′:81°18′ references.)

name: 32-Pillar Shiva Temple
town_description: Barsur is an ancient town in Dantewada district on the banks of the Indravati river, about 75-80 km southwest of Jagdalpur. It was the 11th-century capital of the Nagavanshi (Chindaka Naga) kings, and local tradition credits it with 147 temples and 147 tanks at its zenith. Today it is a quiet rural town whose scattered ASI-protected ruins — the Battisa, Mama-Bhanja and twin-Ganesha temples — make it the richest archaeological zone of Bastar.
